record.title: ODU-Bench reports contextual intent and false-trigger gaps in multimodal assistants
record.summary: Chen et al. introduce ODU-Bench, a benchmark of 2,078 audio and audio-visual demand/no-demand scenes, and report results for 14 native multimodal models. In the paper’s reported evaluation, the best-scoring model recovers 44.7% of key information specifically requiring visual, acoustic or dialogue context; 11 of 14 models trigger on more than half of no-demand scenarios, and Gemini 3.1 Pro triggers on 40.6%. These are author-reported benchmark results, not independently reproduced estimates of real-world assistant behavior.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Chen et al. posted arXiv:2609.21392v1 on 2026-09-18 and define ODU as evaluation of demand presence and contextual demand understanding in audio/audio-visual interactions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that ODU-Bench contains 2,078 scenes: 1,801 synthetic scenarios and 277 human-recorded interactions performed by 30 actors; annotations underwent media-grounded human verification.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In Table 3 and the contextual-recovery analysis, the authors report that Gemini 3.1 Pro recovers 44.7% of key points requiring visual, acoustic or dialogue context and has a 40.6% false-trigger rate on audio-visual no-demand scenes; 11 of 14 evaluated models exceed 50% false-trigger rates across no-demand scenarios.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: These benchmark results do not establish corresponding failure rates in deployed assistants or the expected user harm, nor do they independently validate the benchmark, annotations, or judge scores.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction or audit of ODU-Bench annotations, model outputs, or LLM judge scores was conducted.
The benchmark is challenge-driven and 87% synthetic by scene count; its false-trigger and contextual-recovery rates may not estimate natural deployment traffic.

brief.importance_rationale: If representative, difficulty recovering multimodal intent and avoiding false triggers affects when assistants should act and how safely they handle underspecified speech. The benchmark is a meaningful evaluation contribution, but synthetic-heavy data and unreplicated author-reported results do not establish deployment prevalence.
limitations: Single-group v1 preprint; results are not independently reproduced.
1,801 of 2,078 scenes are synthetic; 277 human-recorded interactions involve 30 actors, so natural traffic and population coverage are not established.
The evaluation uses an LLM judge for key-point matching; appendix diagnostics are author-reported and not independently audited.
The text-only baseline uses a different input interface and is left unranked; not every comparison is matched.
The paper does not establish deployed false-trigger rates, downstream harms, or performance under broad unselected interaction distributions.
brief.summary: Chen et al. introduce ODU-Bench, a benchmark of 2,078 audio and audio-visual demand/no-demand scenes, and report results for 14 native multimodal models. In the paper’s reported evaluation, the best-scoring model recovers 44.7% of key information specifically requiring visual, acoustic or dialogue context; 11 of 14 models trigger on more than half of no-demand scenarios, and Gemini 3.1 Pro triggers on 40.6%. These are author-reported benchmark results, not independently reproduced estimates of real-world assistant behavior.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report 2,078 scenes (1,801 synthetic and 277 human-recorded) and evaluation of 14 native multimodal configurations. The best model’s context-dependent key-point recovery is reported as 44.7%; Gemini 3.1 Pro has a 40.6% false-trigger rate in audio-visual no-demand scenes; 11/14 models exceed 50% false-trigger rate on no-demand cases.
technical.compute_or_cost: No comparable serving cost or latency analysis is claimed in the reviewed result.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1 paper, task definition, dataset composition, evaluation protocol, results table and appendix diagnostics were inspected. No independent execution or reproduction was conducted.
technical.implementation_status: Author-reported arXiv v1 research benchmark with paper-linked dataset and demo; artifacts were not independently downloaded or executed.
technical.mechanism: The benchmark separates demand presence, contextual intent/key-point recovery, temporal localization, transcription and user profile; no-demand examples test whether request-like cues cause false triggering.
technical.regime: ODU-Bench v1, 2,078 scenes, comprising 1,801 synthetic scenarios and 277 human-recorded interactions by 30 actors; 14 native audio/audio-visual model configurations with modality-specific evaluations.
technical.reproducibility: Paper reports human verification of annotations and appendix checks of judge stability and key-point recoverability. Independent reproduction, dataset audit and robustness to less challenge-selected traffic remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares 14 model configurations under a common benchmark and includes a text-only ASR-input baseline that is not ranked because its interface differs. Judge-stability and key-point-recoverability diagnostics are reported in the appendix; independent benchmark audit remains absent.

brief.title: ODU-Bench reports contextual intent and false-trigger gaps in multimodal assistants
brief.why_it_matters: Correctly deciding whether a user has made a request, and recovering intent from context rather than speech alone, is a distinct prerequisite for multimodal assistants. The benchmark reports substantial bounded failures on these behaviors, while its synthetic-heavy composition and judge-based evaluation limit generalization to deployed use.
